title: Elevated-Temperature Tribo-Corrosion Response of Eutectic High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: guess: a cast eutectic high-entropy alloy in the Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni system, designed to produce a lamellar microstructure of disordered FCC and ordered B2/BCC phases
recollection.intervention: guess: high-temperature pin-on-disk tribo-corrosion testing in 3.5 wt % NaCl solution over a temperature range from room temperature up to 600 °C under a 5 N normal load
recollection.structure: guess: retained lamellar eutectic colonies of alternating FCC and B2 phases with oxide tribolayers developed on the sliding surface
recollection.mechanism: guess: synergistic action of high-temperature oxidation and mechanical wear leading to the formation and spallation of mixed metal oxides in the tribolayer, accelerating material removal
recollection.results: guess: friction coefficient rising from ~0.45 at 200 °C to ~0.65 at 600 °C, wear rate increasing from ~1×10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) at 200 °C to ~5×10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) at 600 °C, and a corrosion-wear synergy factor of ~1.5–2.0 at the highest test temperature

score.note: The recalled test geometry and temperature range are wrong, although 5 N was one tested load. The retained lamellar FCC/L12–B2 structure and surface tribolayer formation are substantially correct, despite mislabeling L12 as disordered FCC. The oxidation/spallation mechanism is only generically applicable to the 100 °C regime and omits the key temperature-dependent depassivation–repassivation behavior. All reported friction, wear, temperature, and synergy numbers are incorrect.
